Where things stand on Iran after tense weekend as its delegation leaves Qatar
The Middle East is braced for a possible return to all-out war, with concerns that the United States, along with Israel, could strike Iran shortly after Tuesday's midterm elections in the U.S.
Qatari mediators met with Iranian officials on Sunday for the third consecutive day in an effort to reach a deal to restart direct negotiations between the U.S. and Iran. Iran says there's a two-day plan to stop attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and resume talks with the U.S., depending on the U.S. response.
Trump told reporters on Saturday that negotiations with Iran are "going fine" and noted he is not "in much of a hurry." However, he told a rally in Iowa on Sunday that "the only reason why I'm not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can. But at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer."
